title: Earth and the Moon forming
what: As the aeons begin, a clock in their own time: the Solar System’s first solids, dust gathering into planetesimals and embryos, Earth growing, Theia’s strike, the Moon gathering from the debris, and Earth’s magma ocean cooling to the first ocean.
how: The clock counts tenfolds of time since the first solids up to the impact, then since the impact, so hours and millions of years each get their share. The impact’s date is the one chosen on the rail, and the phases before it are timed from the first solids. Each phase’s words follow its studies; where they disagree, each side is named. Deep time’s moment moves with the clock, so the sketched globe turns from molten to the first ocean as it passes.
others: How fast Earth grew, how the impact went, how fast the Moon gathered and when it all happened are argued, and the clock names the camps rather than choosing between them.
